**About Symmetry**
We’re solving one of the biggest challenges in modern AI workflows: fragmented context. Today, project knowledge is scattered across conversations, tools, and docs—forcing teams to spend more time steering AI than actually getting work done.
  
  
Symmetry brings context, continuity, and observability to AI-powered work, enabling teams to ship faster, work smarter, and maximize productivity across their existing AI stack.
  
  
We’re a fast-moving, early-stage team with a proven track record of building and scaling successful AI businesses. Freshly funded and growing, we’re looking for builders who want to help define the next frontier of human–AI collaboration.
  
  
****Role Summary****
You’ll own the 0→1 systems behind Symmetry’s Intelligence Layer—building the knowledge extraction, mapping, and retrieval systems that transform AI-native work.
  
  
This means experimenting with how to extract, represent, and retrieve knowledge from thousands of conversations—and turning those experiments into working systems that power real user experiences across our API and user-facing features/products.
  
  
If you’re excited by turning product ideas into working LLM systems and iterating through research, data, and prototypes to find what works, you’ll thrive here.
  
  
****What You’ll Build****

* Core AI systems that extract and organize knowledge from AI conversations into structured, reusable context.
* Retrieval and memory infrastructure (GraphRAG + vector search) that delivers precise, low-latency context to user workflows.
* Agentic systems that reason across stored context—handling retrieval, synthesis, and evaluation tasks autonomously.
* Prompt and orchestration frameworks that connect multiple models, tools, and data sources into end-to-end reasoning pipelines.
* Evaluation and telemetry systems to benchmark retrieval quality, latency, and overall intelligence performance.
* Fast prototypes to explore new product directions and validate user-facing capabilities.

****Skills We’re Looking For****

* Strong Python engineering fundamentals—skilled in building performant, maintainable systems and services that connect data, models, and APIs.
* Deep understanding of retrieval architectures—embeddings, vector databases, hybrid or graph-based search, and caching strategies.
* Experience with LLM orchestration frameworks like LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom-built agent systems.
* Proven ability to build and tune LLM-based agents for reasoning, synthesis, or evaluation tasks.
* Familiarity with prompt engineering and multi-step reasoning—designing structured flows that balance quality, latency, and cost.
* Exposure to fine-tuning or adapter training (LoRA, PEFT) and how to integrate tuned models into retrieval pipelines.
* Ability to work end-to-end—backend (FastAPI, Node) to quick front-end demos or dashboards for testing and iteration.
* Comfort operating in open-ended problem spaces, defining your own experiments, and driving them to working outcomes.

If you thrive on autonomy, clarity, and collaboration and want to build the connective tissue between humans and AI systems, Symmetry is where you’ll do your best work.

What if you could get paid to work on the project you've been meaning to build — with a state-of-the-art AI coding assistant at your side, completely free of charge?

* Commitment: Flexible

We work with AI labs that need someone with real engineering experience to judge what their models produce. We're looking for developers who read code the way they read their own: quickly, and with suspicion. Most of the job is reading. You get a task, a model's proposed solution, and sometimes a test suite.

You decide whether the solution is correct, whether the tests prove it, and where the reasoning breaks down. Then you write the verdict in plain language, because a score without an explanation is just an opinion.

You'll also help build the material the model is judged against: edge cases, tricky regressions, prompts that look simple and aren't. The best candidates notice the bug that compiles, passes, and is still wrong. What we need from you:

* 3+ years shipping production code, in any language we can read.
* The habit of checking assumptions instead of trusting a diff.
* Writing clear enough that a stranger can follow your reasoning.
* 10+ hours a week for 6 months or more.

Nice to have: experience reviewing other people's code, a systems or security background, or having maintained something old and fragile. You'll be paid $45 to $55 an hour depending on experience, invoiced twice monthly. Onboarding is paid, and the first two weeks are structured rather than sink-or-swim.

There is no exclusivity, so other contracts are fine as long as the work holds up. If you have ever left a review comment that saved a release, you will recognize this job.

**Job Description**
As an intern in the Quantitative Risk Assessment (QRA) team within System Design & Mission Assurance, you will apply rigorous statistical methods and machine learning techniques to quantify safety and risk across our autonomous driving systems. **In this Role, You Will…**

* Formulate and build statistical and machine learning models to evaluate system performance and analyze rare, high-consequence safety events.
* Process and analyze large-scale datasets using SQL, Python, or distributed data frameworks (Spark/Databricks) to extract actionable insights on vehicle behavior and operational risk.
* Apply advanced statistical methods (e.g., Poisson processes, GLMs, Bayesian inference, point process models, or spatial-temporal modeling) to evaluate safety-critical metrics.
* Collaborate with systems engineers and safety leads to translate complex quantitative models into rigorous mission assurance decisions.

* Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. in Statistics, Data Science, Machine Learning, Computer Science, or a related quantitative engineering/scientific discipline.

* Able to commit to a full-time, 12-week internship beginning in May/June 2027 .
* Ability to relocate to the Bay Area, California, for the duration of the internship.
* Interns at Zoox may not use any proprietary information they are working on as part of their thesis, any published work with their university, or to be distributed to anyone outside of Zoox.

**Qualifications**

* Statistical Foundations: Deep understanding of probability theory, regression, Generalized Linear Models (GLMs), hypothesis testing, and Bayesian methods. Experience or coursework in spatial statistics, space-time models, point process models, or causal inference.
* Machine Learning & Modeling: Strong fundamentals in statistical modeling and ML (supervised and unsupervised learning, model validation, and metric evaluation).
* Data Manipulation & Querying: Proficiency with basic-to-intermediate SQL and Python for data querying, data cleaning, and statistical modeling (or alternative data packages such as Spark, dplyr , or R).
* Communication & Problem Solving: Demonstrated ability to break down ambiguous operational or system questions into structured statistical problems and clearly communicate complex quantitative findings to technical stakeholders.

**Bonus Qualifications**

* Large-Scale Data Processing: Experience querying, pipeline-building, and modeling massive datasets using Spark, Databricks, or cloud platforms.

* AI-Assisted Workflow & Tooling: Experience utilizing AI-assisted data analysis, modern coding agents, or LLM-driven research workflows to accelerate data exploration and model development.

E11 Bio is on a mission to advance connectomics towards the scale of whole mammalian brains. We are a collaborative and interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers engaged in a neuroscience moonshot project to develop a radical technology platform for scalable brain mapping. E11 Bio is a non-profit Convergent Research focused research organization located in Alameda, California, pursuing blue-skies neuroscience research yet operating like a nimble, tight-knit start-up. Read our technology roadmap .
  
  
We are seeking a creative and mission-driven Machine Learning Scientist to develop scalable automatic proofreading methods leveraging barcode and shape information. In this role, you will own core ML pipelines for automated proofreading of neuron and synaptic reconstructions in optical connectomics datasets, working closely with wet lab scientists, microscopists, and domain experts to ensure biological fidelity and scalability. Your work will directly support E11’s goal of making reliable connectomic data accessible to the broader neuroscience community.
  
  
In this role you will be focused on decreasing segmentation and proofreading costs for optical connectomics datasets that we are generating at E11, a critical bottleneck in the connectomics field. You will be responsible for improving initial segmentations using large spatial contexts with rich data features, and ingesting resulting datasets into scalable proofreading software for dissemination to the scientific community.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Contribute to developing innovative ML approaches for automatic proofreading of segmentations in large PB-scale optical connectomics volumes, leveraging shape and barcode information
* Own the deployment of scalable workflows to ingest large connectomic datasets into standard proofreading software (WebKnossos, CAVE)
* Collaborate with academic and industry experts on building and extending tools for automated proofreading and interactive visualization
* Develop, implement, and evaluate scalable pipelines for synapse detection and partner assignment in large-scale optical connectomics datasets, integrating morphological and protein labeling information
* Identify and build ML-based image processing tools that remove key bottlenecks in our data processing and analysis pipeline
* Maintain excellent laboratory science practices, communicate results through reports and presentations, and contribute to and assist in preparation of manuscripts, abstracts and other scientific documents.

**Required Qualifications**

* Ph.D. in computer science, machine learning, applied math, computational biology or a related field in science and/or engineering or Ph.D.-equivalent publication history
* 3-5 years of relevant work or research experience, with strong history of independent and autonomous execution of novel ML solutions
* Strong background in computer vision and applying ML tools to the analysis of large microscopy data sets
* Experience with software engineering best practices (e.g. version control, code reviews, etc)
* Excellent communication and collaboration skills, record keeping ability, and attention to detail

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with graph, sequence, or point based ML methods (GNNs, Transformers, Pointnets, etc.)
* Experience with processing large chunked data (e.g Zarr) in the cloud (e.g. AWS or GCP)
* Experience with large scale connectomics data and tools (e.g. Neuroglancer, WebKnossos, CAVE, CATMAID, etc.)
* Strong record of publications in peer reviewed scientific journals a plus.

**In The First Six Months, You Will**

* Become familiar with our existing ML and distributed processing code bases
* Own the processing (segmentations) of a new dataset end-to-end and identify areas for improvement (accuracy and efficiency)
* Integrate internal graph-based methods for automatic proofreading into standard block-wise workflows for PB-scale optical connectomics volumes
* Optimize ingestion of smaller segmentation graphs into standard proofreading software (e.g WebKnossos, CAVE) for improving efficiency of ground truth generation

**In 12 Months, You Will**

* Develop novel innovative ML approaches for automatic proofreading of neuron segmentations, leveraging both shape and barcode information
* Contribute to algorithmic development across the segmentation pipelines increasing computational throughput
* Contribute to achieving cubic-mm scale reconstruction at 100x lower proofreading costs
* Scale ingestion of PB-sized optical volumes into proofreading software and pilot proofreading and dissemination of large connectomic subgraphs

Our Claims team builds software that helps clinics and hospitals get paid for the care they deliver. We build automations that can be configured to fit each practice's needs, ensuring their entire business pipeline functions smoothly.
  
  
We also build tools that help billers and administrators figure out where their time will have the biggest impact. FDE IIs are autonomous contributors. They deliver working features spanning the full software lifecycle. **Description**
Amazon Software Builder Experience (ASBX), started in 2022, is working to make Amazon the best place to build software. Every day, hundreds of thousands of Amazon software builders rely on us for the tools they build with, and for the technology, training, and community behind them. One of our most important responsibilities is shaping the language ecosystem, both inside Amazon and across the open-source community, to improve the experience for every software builder.
  
  
Our tools are used in all aspects of the business, and their care and evolution are of critical importance to the effectiveness of Amazon. We're looking for a deeply technical leader interested in sustaining and evolving the shared software platform used by nearly every service within the company. Those with experience evolving broadly distributed and highly complex software libraries, such as large open source projects and mission critical foundational software stacks will be given an opportunity to have company wide impact.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
You will design and build developer tools that Amazon engineers use every day. You will work with the languages and libraries that power Amazon's services, making them easier to use and more reliable. You will help maintain our build tools, compilers, libraries and frameworks. You will shape how OSS upstream projects are developing, including contributing to them directly yourself. You will collaborate with engineers across Amazon to understand their pain points and build tools, libraries and frameworks that address them. You will write code, review code from teammates, and help others debug issues with our tools.
  
  
A day in the life
  
  
Your work will directly affect how builders at Amazon do their jobs. We are a language expertise team at the heart of being able to compile and shift software. This is practical work that requires understanding what builders actually need and building tools that solve their problems without getting in the way.
  
  
**About The Team**
The Language Experience team has 3 primary missions. Language toolchains supporting the compiler, package managers, and build tools themselves enabling builders to do their job. Supply chain security and ingestion for 3rd party packages making open source software available to builders in a timely and secure manner. Providing the best developer experience in each support programming language through improvements directly on the language and key packages both inside the company and upstream in open source.

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience

* 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
* 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
* 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
* Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

**Description**
A Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) embeds directly inside a strategic enterprise customer to independently design, build, deploy, and run AI-powered production systems alongside the customer's engineering team. FDE IIs write production-grade software and own delivery of complete AI workstreams end-to-end — from requirements gathering through production deployment — combining the technical rigor of an AWS SDE with the urgency and ownership required to deliver measurable customer business outcomes.
  
  
FDE IIs are autonomous contributors. They deliver working features spanning the full software lifecycle. They design cohesive implementations for well-understood problems, making design trade-offs with appropriate guidance. They take on projects where the business problem is understood but implementations are not fully fleshed out, balancing constraints and limiting short-term workarounds. They coach others on producing high-quality code and train new team members.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Embed within customer engineering teams. Work with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand the business and customer value of the systems you build. Understand the customer's business processes, technical architecture, and operational constraints. Translate customer requirements into technical designs for AI-enabled production systems within your workstream. Requires 30 – 50% travel.
* Build production AI applications. Design and develop production-grade software powering AI and agentic workflows — retrieval pipelines, workflow automation, API orchestration layers, data integration. Solve difficult problems with visible risks or roadblocks, bringing clarity and identifying simple designs for solutions. Integrate foundation models, customer data sources, and existing applications into cohesive AI experiences. Optimize for latency, reliability, and cost.
* Own production for your workstream. Be a significant contributor to the full software development lifecycle including scoping, design, code, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Troubleshoot production incidents across AI models, distributed systems, and application services. Ensure root causes of operational issues are identified and resolved. Implement monitoring, evaluations, guardrails, and CI/CD that keep AI systems healthy. Don't settle for the status quo — routinely identify and execute on opportunities to improve operations.
* Mentor and uplift. Actively mentors and trains new team members on how systems are constructed, operated, and fit into the bigger picture. Coach others on producing high-quality code through mechanisms such as code review. Be active in the code review process, providing meaningful feedback to others.
* Accelerate customer adoption. Identify opportunities to expand AI adoption within your customer engagement. Codify reusable patterns and accelerators that benefit future customer deployments and feed back into AWS services. Make enhancements that improve your team's software and processes.

**Description**
Amazon Web Services (AWS) provides a highly reliable, scalable, low-cost infrastructure platform in the cloud that powers hundreds of thousands of businesses in 190 countries around the world.
  
  
We are hiring an Applied Scientist in our AWS Sales Science & Economics team. The team uses machine learning, econometrics, and data science to optimize AWS’s service catalogue, driving customer engagement and generating insights to guide AWS sales strategy. We use detailed customer behavioral and usage data to predict and understand what customers want from AWS.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
As an Applied Scientist, you will apply the latest research, state of the art machine learning and GenAI to build highly scalable models in support of predictive research and products used across AWS Sales and leadership. You will be responsible for designing and executing science experiments in short and agile cycles. You will use the latest AWS technologies in Machine Learning, Data Science, and AI. You will work closely with business leaders to identify opportunities to drive business growth by applying machine learning and building out predictive models to support analytics and insights.
  
  
The ideal candidate will be curious and able to learn new technologies quickly. You will have hands-on experience building data science and machine learning pipelines in production working with large scale data sets. You are passionate about sharing your knowledge to enable others. You empathize with the needs of our customers and align your work accordingly, and provide thought leadership and guidance across the organization.
  
  
A day in the life
  
  
You will start your day reviewing experimental results and refining model architectures based on new insights. You might spend the morning prototyping a novel approach to a customer-facing problem, then shift to a design review with engineering partners in the afternoon to align on how your solution integrates into production systems. Along the way, you will mentor junior scientists, contribute to peer reviews, and stay connected to the latest research through reading groups and internal science discussions. Your contributions will move from research notebooks to live systems that customers interact with every day.
  
  
**About The Team**
Our team is focused on applying advanced science and machine learning to build intelligent systems that improve the Amazon experience. We value collaboration, intellectual rigor, and a willingness to explore new ideas. You will work alongside scientists and engineers who are committed to turning ambitious research into practical, high-impact solutions. We are investing in the next generation of machine learning capabilities and are looking for team members who are excited to help define that future.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
* Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
* Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in professional software development
* Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining, a PhD in computer science, machine learning, engineering, or related fields
* Have publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
* Experience in solving business problems through machine learning, data mining and statistical algorithms

Kforce has a client in Chicago, IL that is seeking a Python & AI Solutions Developer. Position Summary: We are seeking an experienced Temporary Manager - Risk Technology to support AI, automation, analytics, and technology transformation initiatives within a Credit Review and risk-focused environment. This role will focus on enhancing and scaling existing AI and automation solutions, developing data and document-processing capabilities, and expanding technology-enabled workflows across lending portfolios and business use cases. Key Responsibilities:
  
  

* Enhance, scale, and support existing AI and automation solutions used within credit review workflows
* Extend automation frameworks across additional lending portfolios, risk processes, and business use cases
* Develop Python-based applications, scripts, and automation solutions capable of processing large volumes of structured and unstructured data
* Build and maintain document ingestion, data extraction, and analysis pipelines across PDFs, images, spreadsheets, and other file formats
* Integrate large language models (LLMs) using OpenAI APIs and related technologies to support workflow automation, document analysis, and data processing
* Design solutions that generate structured, traceable, and auditable outputs appropriate for governance, reporting, and review
* Partner with business and risk stakeholders to identify automation opportunities, gather requirements, and translate business needs into scalable technical solutions
* Help drive broader AI, automation, analytics, and process transformation initiatives within the Credit Review Group
* Provide technical leadership and guidance on solution design, scalability, and implementation within a regulated environment

**Requirements**

* Strong hands-on experience developing applications, automation solutions, or data-processing workflows using Python
* Experience building or implementing solutions utilizing AI, machine learning, generative AI, or large language models
* Experience working with OpenAI APIs or similar LLM technologies and integrating them into business applications or workflows
* Experience designing solutions that process both structured and unstructured data, including documents and large datasets
* Demonstrated experience developing and deploying scalable AI or automation solutions within a regulated environment
* Ability to translate business requirements into practical and scalable technical solutions
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to work across technical and business teams
* Ability to operate at a Manager level, balancing hands-on technical execution with solution ownership and stakeholder engagement

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience developing Alteryx workflows and ETL processes
* Experience with Power BI, dashboard modernization, or reporting automation
* Familiarity with financial services, credit risk, credit review, risk management, internal audit, or related environments
* Experience supporting technology transformation or automation initiatives within a financial institution or other highly regulated organization

Ideal Candidate Profile: A strong candidate will be someone who can bridge risk and technology. They should be comfortable getting hands-on with Python, AI/LLM integrations, data, and automation while also working directly with business stakeholders to understand risk processes and determine where technology can improve efficiency, scalability, and consistency.

Design and develop production-grade software powering AI and agentic workflows — retrieval pipelines, workflow automation, API orchestration layers, data integration. Solve difficult problems with visible risks or roadblocks, bringing clarity and identifying simple designs for solutions. Integrate foundation models, customer data sources, and existing applications into cohesive AI experiences. Optimize for latency, reliability, and cost.

**About Peregrine**
Peregrine Advisors is a rapidly growing AI and data innovation hub helping government solve hard problems and deliver better outcomes. We work across the full lifecycle—from strategy and governance through architecture, engineering, analytics, AI, visualization, and training—for clients including the SEC, PCAOB, DDOT, and DCAA.
  
  
Our clients describe our support as "absolutely excellent" and our people as "instrumental to organization's success." Winner of the United Nations COP27 Datathon, our work has earned all Exceptional CPARS ratings, SEC Chair's Awards, the SEC Vision Award, and recognition from FDA leadership.
  
  
We are also built differently. Peregrine is the first and only social enterprise organized as a Benefit Corporation and SBA 8(a) company focused on AI and data for government. We believe business success should create client value, social value, and opportunity for our people.
  
  
As we enter our next stage of growth, we need dependable, motivated, and skilled people who have a combination of intellectual curiosity and intellectual courage. With new clients, larger programs, and expanding responsibilities, the people joining Peregrine now will have the opportunity to help shape the company we become.
  
  
**People first. Ownership always.**
We solve problems through people, process, and technology—in that order. Technology matters, but people make transformation happen. That principle defines our culture. Trust and motivation are the foundational pillars of delivery on which our skills stand. We hire people we can trust, who care deeply about what they do, take ownership, learn quickly, help one another, and refuse to walk past a problem because it belongs to someone else.
  
  
At Peregrine, you are not joining simply to fill a position. You are joining a team, taking ownership of a mission, and helping build a company. If that excites you, we should talk.
  
  
At Peregrine Advisors, you will share in operating the automation, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, and secure cloud infrastructure that keep federal systems running. But we hire people, not seats. As the work evolves, you will move to where the hardest problems are.
  
  
This is a hybrid work arrangement based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area, and the commuting cadence varies by assignment. The initial engagement requires United States citizenship and the ability to obtain a Public Trust determination.
  
  
**Your first project**
Expect your first project to put you shoulder to shoulder with engineers, on pipelines a team leans on every day. Depending on the assignment, you may:
  
  

* Contribute to the Terraform or CloudFormation code that defines infrastructure
* Under senior engineers' guidance, develop and maintain deployment automation and pipelines
* Pitch in on running Docker containers and Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments, from orchestration to monitoring and logging
* Wire vulnerability checks, security scans, and policy controls into the delivery pipeline
* Turn repeatable operational tasks into Python scripts, reaching for Bash or PowerShell when those suit better, and close out every finding that comes back
* Take a hand in mapping and implementing National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-53 (NIST SP 800-53) controls, and automate the evidence that shows compliance
* Bring AI-assisted tools into your pipeline, testing, and scripting work, and verify every output they produce

Code review sees every change you make, and you walk reviewers through the change and your reasons. That is where you learn what makes a change correct, not just that it runs. You automate the team's manual tasks, and you build your share of a practice that designs security in from the start instead of bolting it on later.
  
  
This is where you start, not the shape of your career here.
  
  
**Requirements**

* 1+ years of experience in software development, platform engineering, or operations engineering
* A bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, cybersecurity, engineering, or a related technical discipline
* Practical use of one or more pipeline tools, grounded in a working knowledge of CI/CD concepts
* Ability to write scripts in Python (Bash or PowerShell skills a plus)
* Familiarity with Docker and containerization, together with the cloud services AWS offers
* Exposure to tools that express infrastructure as code, for example CloudFormation or Terraform
* A basic understanding of how containers are orchestrated
* Experience with the fundamentals of Linux
* Knowledge of web applications and application programming interfaces, together with networking concepts and load balancing
* Grounding in the principles of cloud security and in practices for delivering software securely
* Skill at tracking down and resolving problems in infrastructure and in deployments
* Experience generating and reviewing code with AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot
* Proficiency in writing, PowerPoint, and Excel

**Preferred**

* Prior work in information technology for the federal government
* Exposure to one or more of these areas: Authority to Operate (ATO) processes, NIST SP 800-53 controls, or Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) compliance
* An AWS certification or practical experience delivering production workloads on AWS
* A background with security tooling or vulnerability scanning, for example dynamic application security testing (DAST), policy-as-code, or static application security testing (SAST)

**Who You Are**
For you, security and reliability belong in the build from the first commit, never in a final gate, and you are eager to grow into an engineer whose automation replaces other people's manual work and leaves an audit trail. When you hit a wall, you ask rather than guess. Feedback is your fastest way forward, and when priorities move, you move with them. You experiment, fail, learn, and repeat quickly. You would rather own an outcome than be handed a task.
  
  
**What You Bring**

* A grounding in cloud fundamentals, networking, Linux, scripting, and delivery automation, and an appetite to dig deeper into security
* Delivery habits in secure configuration, code review, automated testing, and version control, or a willingness to build them quickly
* Clear, plain updates: what you have finished, where you are stuck, and what you need
* The care to hold up where accuracy and auditability cannot slip

You adapt your development workflow as AI tools evolve, using them to help implement, test, and improve the components you own. You give the tools clear context, review and test their output, and remain accountable for the code you deliver.
  
  
**When we talk**
Be prepared to discuss a difficult problem you worked through, the decisions you made, what happened, and what you learned. The technical assessment is a live Python coding challenge without AI.
  
  
**Benefits**
This is a full-time W-2 position with a salary of $80,000 to $95,000 per year.
  
  
Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance with the employee premium fully paid and half of dependent premiums; employer-paid life, accidental death, and short-term and long-term disability insurance; a 401(k) with an employer match of up to 4% of salary; unlimited paid time off; and sponsored professional certifications and continuing education.
  
  
**What We Offer**
You will work alongside developers, engineers, data scientists, architects, and strategists, on work ranging from strategy to implementation. We support your development across assignments and clients through extensive onboarding, sponsored professional certifications such as the Data Management Capability Assessment Model (DCAM) and AWS technical certifications, and rotation across functions to expand your skills and perspective. The mission is real, the problems are hard, and you own what you ship.
  
  
**What We Commit To**
As a Benefit Corporation, our commitment runs three ways: real, measurable value for our clients; government that works better for the public; and a team that makes everyone in it better.
  
  
We hire people who want to help build the firm, not just work at it. If that is you, apply.

**Who We Are**
Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.
  
  
The Aurora Driver will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.
  
  
At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn.
  
  
**What We Are Looking For**
We're searching for a Summer 2027 Software Engineer Intern for our Vehicle Platforms Team. This role is a unique opportunity for a systems-minded coder to work at the foundational layer of our autonomous trucks, bridging the gap between high-level autonomy software and physical vehicle hardware. You will be instrumental in ensuring our sensors, compute units, and embedded devices function as a seamless, high-performance unit, making this one of the most hands-on software roles at Aurora.
  
  
**In this role you will**

* Integrate Core Hardware Components: Write and maintain C++ interfaces and drivers that integrate Lidars, Radars, Cameras, and other embedded devices into the Aurora Driver stack.
* Support Platform Bring-up: Participate in the initial software "bring-up" of new vehicle platforms, ensuring the onboard compute and sensors are correctly configured and communicating.
* Optimize Onboard Performance: Profile and optimize code to ensure efficient use of limited CPU, GPU, and memory resources on the vehicle.
* Monitor Hardware Health: Develop and refine software tools that track the real-time health and telemetry of our hardware components to ensure safe fleet operations.
* Validate via HIL Infrastructure: Utilize Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) environments to test and verify your code changes against real-world hardware before deployment to the road.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
* Strong proficiency in C++: Solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, and memory management (academic or project-based).
* Hands-on Systems Experience: At least 1–2 years of relevant experience, which can be demonstrated through multiple internships, significant academic research, or professional work involving hardware-software interaction.
* Linux Fundamentals: Experience working in a Linux environment with an understanding of command-line tools and system basics.
* Exposure to Networking Protocols: Familiarity with the basics of data transport, such as TCP/IP, UDP, or serial communication.

**Desirable Qualifications**

* Robotics or Embedded Projects: Experience with ROS/ROS2, microcontrollers (Arduino/STM32/ESP32), or hobbyist robotics.
* Familiarity with Sensors: Prior exposure to Lidar, Radar, or Camera data processing and hardware interfaces.
* Scripting Skills: Proficiency in Python for automation, data analysis, or building internal support tools.
* Automotive Knowledge: Understanding of CAN bus protocols or Automotive Ethernet basics.
* Safety Mindset: Familiarity with concepts of high-availability or safety-critical software design.

**Compensation**
The hourly pay rate for this internship in
**Mountain View**
is:
  
  

* $52.00 per hour for interns pursuing a bachelor’s degree; and
* $58.00 per hour for interns pursuing a master’s degree

**About the Company**

Lightning Rod Labs trains large language models (LLMs) to predict real-world outcomes using scalable self-play on unstructured data. Its platform enables enterprises to train custom models from messy data without requiring extraction. The company has demonstrated that 14B and 32B parameter models trained using its methods can outperform frontier models on prediction-market benchmarks using generated data, without human bottlenecks.

**About the Role**

Lightning Rod Labs is looking for an engineer to build advanced systems that enable AI to reason about real-world outcomes at scale. You will develop infrastructure for prediction agents, work with distributed GPU clusters, transform unstructured data into training signals, and improve model training and evaluation methods. The role covers the full development process, from data collection to deployment.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Build and evolve the infrastructure for training and serving prediction agents.
* Orchestrate distributed training and inference across large, multi-node GPU clusters.
* Convert unstructured data streams into training signals for model learning and evaluation.
* Design training objectives, reward functions, and calibration methods that help models learn causal factors and produce well-calibrated probabilities.
* Optimize training frameworks, fine-tune models, and demonstrate state-of-the-art results on benchmarks.
* Manage delivery across the development lifecycle, from data collection through deployment.

**Required Qualifications**

* Strong Python programming skills and experience fine-tuning large language models.
* A track record of delivering impactful technical systems.
* Ability to take ownership and work autonomously.
* Demonstrated technical skills through GitHub projects, a portfolio, research papers, or demos.
* Experience working beyond small-scale environments, including millions of samples and large distributed GPU clusters.
* Ability to move between rapid notebook-based analysis and robust, scalable data and training pipelines.
* Experience with tools such as Verl, Hugging Face, PyTorch, pandas, and standard training and data-processing tools.
* Strong understanding of statistics, probability, data hygiene, and machine learning best practices.
* Familiarity with cloud platforms, including Modal, GCP, Azure, and AWS.

**What You’ll Get**

* The opportunity to advance methods for training LLMs to make predictions from unstructured data using reinforcement learning and self-play.
* The opportunity to help build a framework aimed at teaching AI things humans do not know.
* Work on critical use cases involving defense, healthcare, and major institutions.
* Ownership of significant parts of the technology stack, from design through delivery.
* A high-trust, fast-paced working environment with autonomy to set direction, deliver frequently, and see the real-world impact of your work.
* Close collaboration with a small team and colleagues across product, engineering, and customer teams, taking projects from research to real-world implementation.

**Location & Work Arrangement**

Remote-first, with a growing hub in Brooklyn, New York City, preferred. Meaningful overlap with Eastern Time is required.

**About the Company**

Nosis Bio is an AI biotechnology company focused on developing treatments for chronic diseases. Founded by Stanford-trained machine learning scientists, molecular biologists, and chemists, the company combines physics-aware deep learning, generative algorithms, and high-throughput biochemical assays to design programmable RNA therapeutics. Nosis Bio is a well-funded, venture-backed startup working with major pharmaceutical companies through multiple partnerships.

**About the Role**

Nosis Bio is seeking a Machine Learning Scientist to advance its physics-aware deep learning platform for designing therapeutics and improving drug delivery. You will develop and improve machine learning architectures and generative algorithms to design complex molecules with targeted chemical and biological properties. Working alongside molecular biologists and biochemists, you will help translate computational designs into experimental results and use new data to improve the platform.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Expand and improve the physics-aware deep learning platform.
* Enhance generative algorithms for molecular design.
* Develop new platform capabilities, including predicting and designing molecules with additional chemical and biological properties.
* Create novel approaches for modeling protein kinetics and dynamics.
* Collaborate with molecular biologists and biochemists to test and refine platform-designed molecules.
* Generate new experimental data to improve machine learning algorithms.

**Required Qualifications**

* PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or Statistics.
* Proven experience inventing and implementing novel deep learning architectures.
* Proficiency in at least one deep learning framework, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX.

**About Peregrine**
Peregrine Advisors is a rapidly growing AI and data innovation hub helping government solve hard problems and deliver better outcomes. We work across the full lifecycle—from strategy and governance through architecture, engineering, analytics, AI, visualization, and training—for clients including the SEC, PCAOB, DDOT, and DCAA.
  
  
Our clients describe our support as “absolutely excellent” and our people as “instrumental to organization’s success.” Winner of the United Nations COP27 Datathon, our work has earned all Exceptional CPARS ratings, SEC Chair’s Awards, the SEC Vision Award, and recognition from FDA leadership.
  
  
We are also built differently. Peregrine is the first and only social enterprise organized as a Benefit Corporation and SBA 8(a) company focused on AI and data for government. We believe business success should create client value, social value, and opportunity for our people.
  
  
As we enter our next stage of growth, we need dependable, motivated, and skilled people who have a combination of intellectual curiosity and intellectual courage. With new clients, larger programs, and expanding responsibilities, the people joining Peregrine now will have the opportunity to help shape the company we become.
  
  
**People first. Ownership always.**
We solve problems through people, process, and technology—in that order. Technology matters, but people make transformation happen. That principle defines our culture. Trust and motivation are the foundational pillars of delivery on which our skills stand. We hire people we can trust, who care deeply about what they do, take ownership, learn quickly, help one another, and refuse to walk past a problem because it belongs to someone else.
  
  
At Peregrine, you are not joining simply to fill a position. You are joining a team, taking ownership of a mission, and helping build a company. If that excites you, we should talk.
  
  
At Peregrine Advisors, you will share in operating the automation, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, and secure cloud infrastructure that keep federal systems running. But we hire people, not seats. As the work evolves, you will move to where the hardest problems are.
  
  
This is a hybrid work arrangement based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area, and the commuting cadence varies by assignment. The initial engagement requires United States citizenship and the ability to obtain a Public Trust determination.
  
  
**Your first project**
Expect Your First Project To Put You Shoulder To Shoulder With Engineers, On Pipelines a Team Leans On Every Day. Depending On The Assignment, You May
  
  

* Contribute to the Terraform or CloudFormation code that defines infrastructure.
* Under senior engineers' guidance, develop and maintain deployment automation and pipelines.
* Pitch in on running Docker containers and Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments, from orchestration to monitoring and logging.
* Wire vulnerability checks, security scans, and policy controls into the delivery pipeline.
* Turn repeatable operational tasks into Python scripts, reaching for Bash or PowerShell when those suit better, and close out every finding that comes back.
* Take a hand in mapping and implementing National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-53 (NIST SP 800-53) controls, and automate the evidence that shows compliance.
* Bring AI-assisted tools into your pipeline, testing, and scripting work, and verify every output they produce.

Code review sees every change you make, and you walk reviewers through the change and your reasons. That is where you learn what makes a change correct, not just that it runs. You automate the team's manual tasks, and you build your share of a practice that designs security in from the start instead of bolting it on later.
  
  
This is where you start, not the shape of your career here.
  
  
**Requirements**

* 1+ years of experience in software development, platform engineering, or operations engineering
* A bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, cybersecurity, engineering, or a related technical discipline
* Practical use of one or more pipeline tools, grounded in a working knowledge of CI/CD concepts
* Ability to write scripts in Python (Bash or PowerShell skills a plus)
* Familiarity with Docker and containerization, together with the cloud services AWS offers
* Exposure to tools that express infrastructure as code, for example CloudFormation or Terraform
* A basic understanding of how containers are orchestrated
* Experience with the fundamentals of Linux
* Knowledge of web applications and application programming interfaces, together with networking concepts and load balancing
* Grounding in the principles of cloud security and in practices for delivering software securely
* Skill at tracking down and resolving problems in infrastructure and in deployments
* Experience generating and reviewing code with AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot
* Proficiency in writing, PowerPoint, and Excel

**Preferred**

* Prior work in information technology for the federal government
* Exposure to one or more of these areas: Authority to Operate (ATO) processes, NIST SP 800-53 controls, or Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) compliance
* An AWS certification or practical experience delivering production workloads on AWS
* A background with security tooling or vulnerability scanning, for example dynamic application security testing (DAST), policy-as-code, or static application security testing (SAST)

**Who You Are**
For you, security and reliability belong in the build from the first commit, never in a final gate, and you are eager to grow into an engineer whose automation replaces other people's manual work and leaves an audit trail. When you hit a wall, you ask rather than guess. Feedback is your fastest way forward, and when priorities move, you move with them. You experiment, fail, learn, and repeat quickly. You would rather own an outcome than be handed a task.
  
  
**What You Bring**

* A grounding in cloud fundamentals, networking, Linux, scripting, and delivery automation, and an appetite to dig deeper into security.
* Delivery habits in secure configuration, code review, automated testing, and version control, or a willingness to build them quickly.
* Clear, plain updates: what you have finished, where you are stuck, and what you need.
* The care to hold up where accuracy and auditability cannot slip.

You adapt your development workflow as AI tools evolve, using them to help implement, test, and improve the components you own. You give the tools clear context, review and test their output, and remain accountable for the code you deliver.

**About the Role**

The University of Rochester is seeking a Data Analyst to support Nursing Finance operations through data collection, analysis, reporting, and financial planning. This role involves analyzing financial, clinical, operational, and nursing performance data from multiple sources to identify trends, variances, and opportunities for improvement.

Working with the Nursing Finance Team and Nursing Practice leaders, the Data Analyst will develop reporting solutions, maintain complex data models and databases, support annual budget planning, and provide insights that inform financial performance and operational decisions.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Report Maintenance and Data Analysis**

* Manage the National Database of Nursing Quality Indicators (NDNQI) submission process for nursing indicators.
* Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot data models, queries, crosswalks, and index files to ensure data accuracy and consistency.
* Extract, validate, and prepare data from systems such as Workday, Axiom, UKG, NPD, and SQL servers for financial and operational reporting.
* Develop and distribute routine reports, including Cost per Patient Day Detail Summary, medical supply purchase reports, manpower reports, and other Nursing Finance analyses.
* Respond to ad hoc data analysis and reporting requests.

**Budget Planning and Fiscal Management**

* Support monthly audit reconciliation, including template management and related reconciliation tasks.
* Develop and maintain gift and education reconciliation file infrastructure.
* Prepare and submit monthly standard journal entries for specific allocations and ledger transaction errors.
* Support annual budget preparation by developing data models, generating reports, reviewing plan files, and validating information in Axiom and related systems.
* Submit basic FTE and budget modification requests.
* Track the team's FTE and budget modification submissions, including complex data validation and reconciliation, to ensure consistency across reporting systems.

**Data Integrity and Quality Control**

* Ensure data accuracy and consistency across relevant systems and sources.
* Maintain the integrity and structure of assigned databases and data files.
* Monitor data processes and reporting methodologies to identify opportunities to improve accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and automation.
* Protect confidential patient, employee, and financial information.
* Document data sources, transformations, analytical methodologies, report logic, and standard operating procedures to support consistent reporting processes.

**Collaboration and Support**

* Provide clean, validated data and analysis for departmental reporting, financial projections, and strategic initiatives.
* Collaborate with departments and stakeholders to support efficient and accurate data flow.
* Serve as a resource for nursing departments on UR Financials tasks and processes.
* Support internal and external audits by compiling, validating, and verifying required data and documentation and assisting with discrepancy resolution.
* Develop data analyses, reports, dashboards, and presentations for Nursing Finance, Nursing Practice leadership, and executive audiences.
* Assist the Director of Nursing Practice Finance and Senior Financial Analyst in preparing the annual Nursing operating budget presentation.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in statistical analysis, database management, or related studies, along with three years of data analysis or customer resource management systems experience.
* An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
* Strong attention to detail.
* Accuracy and record-keeping skills.
* Data analysis and problem-solving abilities.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas.
* Foundational understanding of data modeling concepts or experience managing relational databases.

**Preferred Qualifications and Skills**

* Healthcare experience.
* Ability to learn and navigate multiple software platforms, including UR Financials, UKG, Axiom, and clinical databases.
* Strong organizational, data analysis, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to communicate data visually through dashboards, charts, reports, and presentations.
* Ability to collaborate with stakeholders across departments and translate business needs into analytical and reporting solutions.

Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.
  
  
At Toast, we are committed to empowering our customers by providing the technology, resources, and community they need to thrive. While our roots are in food service, we are rapidly expanding into adjacent markets and international territories. Our mission is to build a world-class Device Management platform that supports the diverse needs of all Toast customers, regardless of their industry or location.
  
  
As a frontend engineer on the Android Systems team, you will build the web experiences that sit on top of the foundational platform for Toast POS devices. Whether it’s an international team looking to deploy a new on-device application, a customer needing a critical firmware update, an Enterprise group needing multi-location device tooling - our web tools empower customers and Toast teams to set up, secure, and manage their devices from wherever they are.
  
  
**Why this team?**

* Expanding the Vision: We are expanding our Mobile Device Management ecosystem—unifying firmware, on-device apps, and security controls into one cohesive platform.
* Frictionless Device Management: We are transforming the customer’s device lifecycle experience from out-of-the-box setup to continuous remote management, leveraging AI to dramatically reduce operator’s time spent troubleshooting and configuring devices.

***About this roll\* (Responsibilities):***

* Hands-on design and implementation of web applications in React and TypeScript that power Toast's device management suite, including device configuration, policy management, and firmware and app update tooling.
* Collaborate with Product Management, Hardware, QA, and other Software teams to build scalable systems, making solid technical decisions with quality, security, and maintainability in mind.
* Partner with UX to turn designs into accessible, responsive, and performant interfaces using Toast's design system.
* Write automated unit, integration, and end-to-end tests to keep our web apps reliable as they grow.
* Deploy features out to customers using feature flags, monitor for success, and help investigate and fix production issues.
* Leverage cutting edge AI tools to enhance your development workflow, improve velocity, and help pioneer new approaches to building, contributing to a culture of innovation and productivity across the team.

***Do you have the right ingredients\*? (Requirements):***

* 3+ years of professional frontend web development experience.
* Clear written and verbal communication.
* Proficient in React, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, with experience building responsive single-page applications.
* Understanding of component architecture and state management.
* Experience integrating with REST or GraphQL APIs.
* Experience writing tests with frameworks such as Jest, React Testing Library, or Playwright.
* Proficiency with source control and code review tools such as Git or GitHub.
* Passion for clean, maintainable code and thoughtful user experiences.
* Strong customer empathy and a drive to build tools that make restaurant operators' lives easier.

***Bonus ingredients\*:***

* Experience working with design systems or shared component libraries.
* Experience working in large, multi-team frontend codebases or micro-frontend architectures.
* Experience with GraphQL clients and data-fetching libraries such as Apollo or React Query.
* Some backend experience in Java or Kotlin, or an interest in learning.
* Interest in hardware, Android, or mobile device management (MDM) concepts.
* Familiarity with AI-augmented development workflows and tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, or similar).

***What we use to make our dish\* (Our Tech Stack):***

* React and TypeScript micro-frontends built on Toast's in-house design system.
* GraphQL and REST APIs, using modern data-fetching and state management libraries.
* Automated testing with Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, and Playwright.
* Kotlin backend services built on AWS that manage device policies, firmware updates, and device configuration.
* Android system apps in Kotlin running on Toast's POS devices.
* Feature flags and production monitoring to ship safely to customers.

**Description**
Sponsored Products and Brands (SPB) helps millions of advertisers reach shoppers across Amazon's stores worldwide. Behind every ad we show are machine learning models that predict click-through rate (CTR) and conversion rate (CVR). These predictions decide which ads are relevant, how they rank, and how advertisers get value.
  
  
Our team builds and runs the ML infrastructure behind those models, end to end:
  
  

* Offline feature engineering: a multi-tenant platform used by several ML teams. It runs thousands of daily feature jobs over petabyte-scale data and produces the features that train models in every marketplace we serve.
* Model training: the standard system that retrains CTR and CVR models every day. How fresh these models are directly affects advertiser results and Amazon's revenue.
* Online feature store and feature retrieval: low-latency, high-throughput services that provide features when a model makes a prediction. These predictions feed the scores used in real-time ad ranking.
* Next-generation research platform: a platform that uses AI agents to help scientists explore, test and launch new model ideas faster.

As an SDE II, you'll design, build and run distributed systems that work at very large scale, both in offline batch processing and online serving. You'll work closely with applied scientists and engineers to make models fresher, help scientists try ideas faster, and keep the systems that support ads ranking reliable.

* Improve the scalability, automation and efficiency of large-scale training and real-time inference systems
* Work closely with applied scientists to optimize the performance of ML models and infrastructure, and take models from experimentation into production
* Deliver ML solutions end to end: design, implementation, testing, deployment and operations
* Collaborate with engineers and scientists across the team to build systems that serve ads across all Amazon platforms and surfaces
* Participate in design and code reviews and mentor peers

Our team — Quick Core Experience — owns the platform layer behind Amazon Quick, an agentic, AI-powered digital workspace. This role offers wide scope, real ownership, and the chance to shape Enterprise governance layers we add in Quick, that every team in the product depends on.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Lead the design and implementation of distributed systems, providing system-wide architectural guidance
* Build Agents to ease on-boarding and evaluation of Enterprise governance across Quick features and Quick accounts.

* Drive adoption of engineering best practices and operational excellence across the team
* Solve complex technical problems with multiple risks and roadblocks, bringing clarity through simple, well-designed solutions
* Mentor and coach multiple engineers, helping develop the next generation of technical talent

Effectively communicate technical designs to both technical and non-technical audiences

* 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
* 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
* Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language

* 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience

**Description**
The Amazon Optics Video team is looking for a Software Development Engineer to build and operate the core video services that secure Amazon's physical sites worldwide. You will design, develop, and maintain production services that power video streaming, recording, and camera management for over 300,000 cameras globally.
  
  
Your work directly protects every Amazon data center, corporate office, and facility. You will build systems that enable security operators to stream live video, record continuously, manage cameras at scale, and extract image frames on demand.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
Design, implement, and deploy features across nine (9) production video services including cloud-based streaming, continuous recording, on-premises recording, camera lifecycle management, and image extraction.
  
  
Write clean, maintainable, and well-tested code in a production environment serving security-critical workloads.
  
  
Participate in on-call rotations and drive operational excellence for video infrastructure across all regions.
  
  
Collaborate with customer groups spanning Data Center Security, Security Operations Centers, Analytics, and infrastructure teams.
  
  
Contribute to architecture decisions across cloud and edge computing, working with services spanning AWS (S3, CloudFront, ECS, EC2, Kinesis) and embedded applications running on camera hardware.
  
  
Drive automation to reduce operational burden. Every feature must reduce the number of humans required to onboard or troubleshoot a site.
  
  
Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and operational readiness reviews.

The Video team sits within Amazon Optics, the organization responsible for physical security technology across all Amazon sites. **Who Are We?**
Postman is the world’s leading API platform, used by more than 45 million+ developers and 500,000 organizations, including 98% of the Fortune 500. Postman is helping developers and professionals across the globe build the API-first world by simplifying each step of the API lifecycle and streamlining collaboration—enabling users to create better APIs, faster.
  
  
The company is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Boston, New York, Austin, Tokyo, London, and Bangalore - where Postman was founded. Postman is privately held, with funding from Battery Ventures, BOND, Coatue, CRV, Insight Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. Learn more at postman.com or connect with Postman on X via @getpostman.
  
  
P.S: We highly recommend reading The "API-First World" graphic novel to understand the bigger picture and our vision at Postman.
  
  
**About The Team**
We are building a small, exceptional Frontier AI Engineering team at Postman.
  
  
The idea is pretty simple. Some of the most important problems in AI are not solved in a lab or in a planning meeting. They are solved when great engineers sit with customers, understand what they are trying to build, see where things break, and help make it work.
  
  
**The Opportunity**
Frontier AI Engineers will work directly with some of our most ambitious customers to design, build, and bring real AI and agentic systems into production.
  
  
This is a hands-on engineering role. You will write code, build prototypes, debug systems, make architecture decisions, and work side by side with customer engineering teams to get things running.
  
  
You might be working on an agent that needs reliable tool use, an MCP based integration, a RAG pipeline that needs better retrieval quality, an evaluation framework for production agents, model routing across multiple LLM providers, or the identity and policy layer required to safely let agents take actions.
  
  
The work spans the full AI stack, from models and inference to agents, APIs, tools, context, evaluation, security, observability, and production infrastructure.
  
  
Just as importantly, you will bring what you learn back into Postman.
  
  
We do not want to build a collection of one off solutions. We want to understand the hard AI engineering problems our customers are running into, recognize the patterns that repeat, and turn those lessons into product capabilities that can help thousands of other developers.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Build real AI systems. Work with LLMs, agents, MCP, APIs, tool calling, RAG, vector search, structured outputs, multimodal models, and production AI workflows.
* Design agentic systems. Build agents that can reason across tools, APIs, enterprise data, and workflows while maintaining the right controls around identity, permissions, policy, and execution.
* Work across the model layer. Experiment with leading foundation models, model routing, inference, prompt and context engineering, fine tuning where it makes sense, and the tradeoffs between quality, latency, cost, and reliability.
* Make AI measurable. Build evaluation systems for agents and LLM applications, including task success, tool correctness, hallucination detection, regression testing, safety, latency, and cost.
* Make AI production ready. Work on observability, tracing, guardrails, fallback strategies, rate limits, retries, caching, model gateways, and the infrastructure needed to operate AI systems reliably at scale.
* Solve the context problem. Help customers reason about retrieval, memory, grounding, context windows, embeddings, vector databases, enterprise data, and how the right context gets to the right model or agent at the right time.
* Secure agent actions. Work on authentication, authorization, secrets, API access, policy enforcement, human approval, auditability, and the controls required when AI systems can actually take actions.
* Own problems end to end. Start with a problem that may not be clearly defined and take it from architecture to prototype to evaluation to production.
* Stay close to the code. We are looking for builders. You will prototype, integrate, debug, experiment, benchmark, and ship.
* Work with ambitious engineering teams. Spend time with AI teams, platform teams, developers, and engineering leaders who are pushing the boundaries of what they can build.
* Shape what Postman builds next. The problems you see in the field will directly influence our AI platform, APIs, Gateway, identity, agent capabilities, developer experience, and product roadmap.
* Turn learning into a product. Identify patterns that repeat across customers and turn them into reusable primitives, reference architectures, workflows, and platform capabilities.
* Help define Frontier AI Engineering at Postman. We are early. The first engineers who join will help define the technical bar, architecture, engineering practices, operating model, and culture of the team.

**About You**

* We are looking for people who are deeply technical and love building.
* People who are just as comfortable opening a terminal and debugging an agent trace as they are sitting with another engineering team and working through an architecture.
* People who understand that building with LLMs is not just about writing prompts. It is about systems engineering, evaluation, reliability, data, APIs, security, and everything required to make probabilistic systems behave predictably in production.
* People who are curious about where models are going, but equally interested in what it takes to make them useful today.
* People who like hard problems and do not need everything perfectly defined before they start building.
* Your background might be in applied AI, agentic systems, AI infrastructure, distributed systems, developer platforms, APIs, security, ML infrastructure, inference, or model platforms.
* What matters more is how you think and how you build.
* We care about strong engineering fundamentals, AI fluency, technical depth, curiosity, judgment, speed, and ownership.
* Above all, we want engineers who want to be close to where AI is actually being built and put into production.

If you want to build agents and AI systems that move beyond demos into real production environments, solve hard engineering problems, and help define Frontier AI Engineering at Postman, we would love to talk.

**Location:**
Cambridge, MA - In Person

**Type:**
Full-time

$160,000–$220,000 + equity

**Who we are**

Today, AI is something you rent. Alpaca is building the full stack of hardware, software, models, and applications together to make it something you own.

We are developing a new computer architecture that breaks the economics keeping frontier models trapped in datacenters. On top of that, we’re building a platform of models, applications, and services that give that hardware meaning.

Personal AI is moving from the datacenter to the desk, and we are driving that change.

Our team is based in Cambridge, MA.

**About the role**

We are looking for master's and PhD graduates with strong fundamentals in digital IC design and substantial hands-on experience in ASIC physical implementation through research, internships or tapeout projects.

You will contribute to the physical implementation of Alpaca's ASIC designs, from synthesis through place and route and timing closure. Starting with well-defined blocks, you will analyze timing, congestion and power, implement improvements, and develop scripts that make the design flow reproducible. You will work closely with the silicon team and take increasing ownership of block implementation as you build experience.

This is a full-time, on-site role at our Cambridge office, starting in 2027.

**What you will do**

* Implement assigned blocks through synthesis, floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis and routing, using static timing analysis to guide timing closure.
* Analyze timing, congestion, area and power results; implement changes and measure their effects.
* Write Tcl and Python scripts to automate implementation steps, reproduce runs and summarize results.
* Contribute to SRAM macro placement, power-grid planning and physical verification for memory-intensive blocks.
* Work with RTL, verification and architecture engineers to understand how design choices affect physical implementation.
* Document results and unresolved issues, participate in design reviews, and take increasing responsibility for block deliverables.

**Minimum qualifications**

* A master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or a related field, completed or expected between December 2026 and June 2027.
* Substantial hands-on ASIC physical design experience through research, coursework or an internship, with clear personal responsibility for implementation and debugging.
* Experience taking a design from RTL or a netlist through place and route to a DRC-clean layout and closing timing, using Cadence, Synopsys or an open-source flow such as OpenROAD.
* Strong foundations in digital IC design, VLSI and computer architecture, including CMOS logic, synchronous design, setup and hold timing, clocking and interconnect delay.
* Programming skills in Python and Tcl, and comfort working in Linux.
* Strong analytical and debugging skills, with the ability to explain implementation results, design tradeoffs and your own contributions clearly.

**Preferred qualifications**

* Contributions to a chip tapeout, with clear ownership of physical implementation tasks.
* Research in VLSI, physical design, EDA or computer architecture involving implemented and evaluated designs or tools.
* An internship in physical design, timing, verification or CAD.
* Experience with SRAM macros, power-grid planning, physical verification (DRC/LVS) or low-power design.
* Experience with open-source tools such as OpenROAD, Yosys, OpenSTA, KLayout or Magic.

**How to apply**

Send us your resume, GitHub, and some projects you have worked on, along with a short note about why Alpaca interests you.

More than credentials, we want to see what you've made, researched, designed, or shipped.

If the role sounds like you but your background is unconventional, apply anyway.

Government technology has failed citizens, veterans, public servants, and service members for decades.
  
  
Kaizen powers America’s application layer. We replace the legacy systems federal agencies run on with modern software, built with craft. The ticketing platform a resident uses to visit a presidential library. The marketplace DoW uses to procure counter-drone systems to protect lives and critical infrastructure. The system a Veteran uses to access benefits. We build systems of record, of national consequence. Our AI-native modules and harness allow us to do so in weeks, not years.
  
  
This year, our revenue has grown 35x. Next year, our software will serve over 100 million Americans across dozens of federal agencies.
  
  
Founded in 2022 and based in New York City and DC, Kaizen has raised $35 million from NEA, a16z, Accel, 776, and Carpenter Capital.
  
  
**Location**
New York, NY (Hybrid). In office Monday to Thursday. Candidates must live in or be able to commute to New York City.
  
  
**The Role**
Most companies building with AI connect someone else's models to their software. Kaizen's AI-native platform turns requirements into working applications, and today much of that intelligence comes from general-purpose models that carry capabilities we don't need, lack knowledge we do, and leave us and our customers paying frontier-model token costs for intelligence we don't control. This role changes that. You'll fine-tune, adapt and distill open-weight models into specialized intelligence Kaizen owns, and prove where it beats the general-purpose alternative. The goal isn't the biggest model or the most papers: it's public-sector software that works better, costs less to run, and is harder to replicate.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Fine-tune, adapt and distill open-weight models for requirements interpretation, code generation, repository understanding, structured output and software validation.
* Own the experiment loop: curate datasets, build training pipelines, and test architectures and techniques until a promising idea becomes a working model.
* Build evaluations on real software engineering tasks that set baselines, expose failure modes, and separate real gains from benchmark noise.
* Work with platform engineers to find where current models fall short, then build the capabilities that close those gaps and ship them into production.
* Experiment with supervised fine-tuning, synthetic data, preference optimization and reinforcement learning to improve model behavior on specialized tasks.
* Deliver applications built around each customer's needs without frontier-model token spend, so public budgets go to residents, not inference.
* Lay the groundwork (datasets, evals, research practices) for Kaizen to eventually train its own models from scratch.

**What You'll Bring**

* Hands-on experience training, fine-tuning or adapting language models. You've worked with model weights, not just model APIs or prompts.
* Strong software engineering fundamentals. You build reliable training pipelines, debug complex systems, and write code other engineers build on.
* Strong Python and PyTorch, with a working understanding of transformer architectures, tokenization and language model training.
* Something you've built that shows real model engineering ability: a fine-tuned model, an original training approach, or a meaningful open-source ML contribution. Industry, research or independent work all count; demonstrated ability matters more than years or credentials.

**Strong Candidates May Also...**

* Have fine-tuned models for code generation, program synthesis or repository understanding.
* Design experiments and evaluation sets that tell a meaningful improvement from noise or overfitting.
* Bring experience with synthetic data, distillation, quantization, or preference optimization and RL with verifiable rewards.
* Have contributed to open-source model development, published applied ML research, or reproduced significant research results.

**Don't Apply If...**

* Your model experience is prompt engineering and API calls.
* You'd rather publish a result than ship a model people use every day.
* You hand off notebooks and expect someone else to make them run in production.
* You assume the biggest model is the right answer and don't want to think about cost.

Residents and public servants rely on the software we build because they don't have another option. The models underneath it have to earn that.
